title: add invocation mesh fidelity metrics and oriented alert slicer
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: We've been seeing noisy SLO alerts caused by multi-stage invocation patterns where kernel queueing and KV-cache warmup dominate tail latency and token cost. This PR introduces a lightweight "invocation mesh fidelity" signal that correlates per-invocation phase coverage (prefetch/warmup/steady/evict) with token-level cost and a new oriented alert slicer that can produce candidate quieting rules for oncall and alerting pipelines. Motivation: Reduce alert churn and enable SREs/product engineers to debug long-tail cost regressions by slicing alerts along invocation-phase fidelity and kernel-queue-pressure dimensions. Goals: (1) Surface a compact set of per-invocation fidelity histograms (phase coverage, warmup hit rates), (2) Add an alert-slice builder that suggests suppression candidates when a majority of high-cost samples are warmup-dominated, (3) Add a dashboard and runbook links for triage. Checklist: - [x] Collector: add fidelity fields to the invocation protobuf and exporter (observability-pack/collectors/mesh_fidelity/collector.go) - [x] Metrics: implement phase_coverage, warmup_hit_ratio, kernel_queue_pressure gauges and token_cost_by_phase histogram - [x] Tracing: enrich spans with fidelity tags and add a compact span summary for drilldown - [x] Alerting: oriented-alert-slicer service that ingests sampled traces and emits suggested alert filters - [x] Dashboard: new 'Invocation Mesh' dashboard with sparkline panels and phased cost stack - [x] Tests: unit tests for exporter and e2e replay with synthetic tracebench - [x] Docs: short runbook + API notes in observability-pack/docs/invocation-mesh.md What changed (high level): - Introduced a mesh_fidelity exporter that attaches phase annotations to invocations; the exporter is conservative (defaults to "unknown") and is opt-in via config. - Added three primary metrics: invocation_phase_coverage{phase}, invocation_warmup_hit_ratio, kernel_queue_pressure_samples and a histogram token_cost_phase_bucketed to allow per-phase cost attribution. - Added a lightweight oriented-alert-slicer binary that analyzes a recent window of sampled spans and returns a ranked list of alert-suppression candidates (e.g., "suppress if warmup_hit_ratio < 0.3 AND kernel_queue_pressure > 0.8"). - New Grafana dashboard (observability-pack/dashboards/invocation-mesh.json) with panels for phase coverage, per-phase token-cost waterfall, and an alert suggestion panel that links to the slicer UI. - Small updates to the trace sampler to ensure we include fidelity headers for span rehydration in logs for the synthetic replay. Backwards compatibility: exporter emits new tags but preserves existing fields; older collectors ignore the extra tags. Operational notes: the slicer runs as a best-effort periodic job; suggested filters are not applied automatically. See runbook for recommended thresholds and how to adopt suggestions. Risks/Mitigations: - Incorrect phase classification could lead to bad suggestions; mitigated by conservative defaults and a "confidence" field included with each suggestion. - Additional metric cardinality: phase is low-cardinality (prefetch/warmup/steady/evict/unknown) and we aggregate before export. Testing: included unit tests for classification heuristics and a small replaybench that validates token-cost attribution on synthetic warmup-heavy traces. Rollout: feature gated behind observability.enable_mesh_fidelity (false by default) and an opt-in dashboard import. Related: ENG-983 (alert quieting), ENG-1142 (kernel queue tracing), SUP-4021 (customer-reported warmup alerts).

release_notes: Added invocation mesh fidelity metrics (phase coverage, warmup hit ratio, kernel queue pressure), a new invocation-mesh dashboard, and an oriented alert slicer to suggest alert-suppression rules for warmup-dominated noise. Feature is opt-in and disabled by default.
notes_for_oncall: If you receive an alert with suggested suppression from the slicer, validate against sample_ref footprints in the dashboard and only apply suggestions that have confidence >= 0.85. The slicer suggestions are only hints; do not auto-apply.
